source: Authored by hand. Every target was chosen by reading the numbered section headings extracted from the current textbook PDFs in public/ncert/, not by matching chapter titles. See data/exemplar-chapter-map.md for the reasoning behind each row.
note: NCERT Exemplar book codes (ieep1, ieep2) are not textbook codes and appear in no manifest. This file is the only bridge between an Exemplar unit and a chapter of the book a Class 9 student actually has. A null target means the unit has no honest home in the current book; its questions are dropped rather than filed somewhere plausible.

mappings.why: States of matter, interconversion, latent heat and the kelvin scale are not taught anywhere in iesc1. The word 'latent' appears nowhere in the thirteen chapters; 'states of matter' appears once, in iesc1 ch5, as a pointer to further reading. Rationalisation moved this material out of Class 9.
evidence: iesc105 line 1253: 'To learn more about the states of matter and concentration of solutions,' - a cross-reference, not coverage

mappings.why: Section for section: 5.1 How Can We Classify Mixtures?, 5.2 Solutions, 5.3 Methods of Separation of Homogeneous Mixtures, 5.4 separating the components of a mixture, 5.5 Tyndall Effect. Colloid, suspension and sublimation occur only in this chapter.

9.1 Law of Conservation of Mass, 9.2 Law of Constant Proportions, 9.3 Dalton's Atomic Theory, 9.4 How Atoms Combine?, 9.5 Writing Chemical Formulae, 9.7 Molecular Mass of Covalent Compounds, 9.8 Formula Unit Mass of Ionic Compounds - the Exemplar unit's contents in the same order.
mappings.caveat: The mole concept and Avogadro's number are in the Exemplar unit but not in iesc1 ch9 ('mole' and 'avogadro' get zero hits). Questions on moles are correctly filed by topic but are beyond the current syllabus.

mappings.why: 8.2 A Short Historical Journey Through Atomic Models, 8.4 Symbols of Elements, 8.5 Atomic Number, 8.6 Mass Number, 8.7 how electrons are distributed in shells, 8.8 Valency, 8.9.1 Isotopes.

target.chapterTitle: Cell: The Building Block of Life

mappings.why: 2.1 How to Study Cells?, 2.2 Structure of a Cell, 2.5 Cell Theory - The Unifying Principle of Biology. Prokaryotes, eukaryotes and the organelles are covered here and nowhere else.
3.1 Why are Plant and Animal Tissues Different?, 3.2 Tissues for Growth in Plants, 3.3 Animal Tissues. Meristem, xylem and phloem are taught here.

4.1 Motion in a Straight Line, 4.2 Graphical Representation of Motion, 4.3 Kinematic Equations for Motion in a Straight Line, 4.4 Motion in a Plane.
6.1 The Concept of Force, 6.2 Balanced and Unbalanced Forces, 6.3 The Force of Friction, 6.4-6.6 Newton's three laws, 6.7 Forces Acting on a System of Objects.

The universal law of gravitation, free fall, g, thrust, pressure and Archimedes' principle have no chapter in iesc1. 'universal law', 'free fall', 'thrust' and 'archimedes' all get zero hits. Buoyancy survives only as a paragraph inside iesc1 ch6 on kinds of force, which is not enough to file a whole unit against.
evidence: iesc106 lines 63, 103, 108 - buoyant force mentioned within 6.1 The Concept of Force

mappings.why: 7.1 Work Done by a Constant Force, 7.2 The Work-Energy Theorem, 7.3 Forms of Energy, 7.4 Mechanical Energy, 7.5 Power.
10.1 Production of Sound, 10.2 Propagation of Sound, 10.3 Sound Waves, 10.5 Graphical Representation of a Sound Wave, 10.6 Characteristics of a Sound Wave, 10.7 Reflection of Sound.

There is no health-and-disease chapter in iesc1. 'antibiotic', 'vaccin' and 'infectious' occur only as passing words inside other chapters; no section covers disease, its causes, prevention or immunity.
evidence: 'pathogen' hits only iesc112, in one sentence about parasitic worms
'vaccin' hits iesc102 line 943 and iesc111 line 942, both incidental

target.chapterTitle: Earth as a System: Energy, Matter, and Life

mappings.why: 13.1 Uneven Heating of the Earth, 13.2 Uneven Heating Causes Wind and Ocean currents, 13.3 Biogeochemical Cycles, 13.4 Human Impact on Earth's Processes. Ozone, the greenhouse effect and the nitrogen cycle occur only here.
mappings.caveat: Medium rather than high: the Exemplar unit also carries soil formation and soil erosion, which the NCF chapter treats far more lightly. Those questions are on-topic for the chapter but not necessarily examinable from it.

mappings.why: Crop production, manure and fertilisers, animal husbandry and cropping patterns have no chapter in iesc1. 'husbandry' gets zero hits; the one 'irrigation' occurrence is a discussion prompt inside the tissues chapter.

3.3 Integers: Expanding the Horizon, 3.4 Fractions and Rational numbers, 3.5 Irrational Numbers, 3.6 Real Numbers: Decimals and Cyclic Patterns. Same material, same order.

Re-cut across two chapters and partly dropped. Degree and zeroes now live in iemh1 ch2, but only for linear polynomials; the identities and factorisation live in iemh1 ch4. The remainder theorem and the factor theorem - a large share of the Exemplar unit - are gone entirely. There is no single chapter this unit belongs to.
evidence: iemh1 ch2 is titled 'Introduction to Linear Polynomials'; headings 2.2 Linear Polynomials, 2.3 Exploring linear patterns
iemh1 ch4 headings 4.2 Visualising Identities, 4.5 and 4.6 Factorisation

target.chapterTitle: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

mappings.why: 1.2 Settling In (the cartesian plane, axes, quadrants, plotting) and 1.4 Distance Between Two Points in the 2-D Plane. Abscissa, ordinate and quadrant questions land squarely here.
2.5 Linear Relationships and 2.6 Visualising linear relationships are exactly the graph of a linear equation in two variables, and the chapter's own exercises use that phrase.
evidence: iemh102 line 359 '2.5 Linear Relationships', line 415 '2.6 Visualising linear relationships'
iemh102 line 854 uses the phrase 'a linear equation in two variables (work w and distance d)'
mappings.caveat: Medium rather than high: the NCF chapter approaches this through linear polynomials and their graphs, so Exemplar questions phrased purely in 'ax + by + c = 0' formalism sit slightly outside how the chapter presents it.

mappings.why: Axiomatic geometry is gone from Class 9. 'Euclid', 'axiom' and 'postulate' get zero hits across all eight chapters of iemh1.
No chapter covers parallel lines, transversals or the angle sum property. 'transversal', 'vertically opposite' and 'angle sum' get zero hits.

Triangle congruence (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS) is not taught in iemh1. 'congruent triangles' gets zero hits; the only 'congruen' matches are about congruent regions in the circles and area chapters, which is a different idea.
There is no quadrilaterals chapter and no midpoint theorem. 'quadrilateral' appears only inside the circles and area chapters as a shape being used, not as a topic with its own properties and proofs.
6.6 Area of a Rectangle, 6.7 Area of a Parallelogram, 6.8 Area of a Triangle, and the chapter argues the same-base-same-height result the Exemplar unit is built on.
evidence: iemh106 line 533: 'ABCD) with the same base b and same height h'
mappings.caveat: Medium rather than high: the Exemplar unit states its results as formal theorems about figures on the same base and between the same parallels; the NCF chapter reaches the same facts by dissection rather than by proof.

target.chapterTitle: I'm Up and Down, and Round and Round

mappings.why: The title says nothing, the sections say everything: 5.1 Definitions, 5.2 Symmetries of a Circle, 5.4 Chords and the Angles They Subtend, 5.5 Midpoints and Perpendicular Bisectors of Chords, 5.6 Distance of Chords from the Centre, 5.7 Angles Subtended by an Arc, 5.8 Concyclicity of Points. This is the Class 9 circles chapter.

Ruler-and-compass construction of bisectors and triangles is not a chapter in iemh1. The only 'compass' and 'ruler and' hits are in ch3, about locating an irrational number on the number line - a different task.
Section 6.8.1 is literally 'Heron's formula', with worked examples using the semi-perimeter.
evidence: iemh106 lines 701, 736, 766 - worked examples using s, the semi-perimeter

mappings.why: iemh1 ch6 is two-dimensional throughout - perimeter and area. Solids are gone: 'surface area', 'cylinder' and 'cone' get zero hits across iemh1.

A merged unit whose halves went different ways. Probability is iemh1 ch7, but statistics - class marks, class intervals, frequency distributions, histograms, mean, median and mode - has no chapter at all, and the unit's single MCQ exercise runs both together (Q1-Q27 statistics, Q28-Q30 probability). Filing the unit anywhere mis-files most of it, and splitting it by keyword would be a guess about each question rather than a fact about the book.
evidence: iemh1 ch7 headings 7.1-7.4 are probability only
ieep214 EXERCISE 14.1 Q1-Q27 are class marks, frequency tables, mean, median and mode
mappings.caveat: The probability tail of EXERCISE 14.1 could be recovered by hand into iemh1 ch7 by a teacher who reads each question. This extractor will not do it automatically.

Same chapter under the same name, renumbered from 8 to 7. Section 7.3 SEXUAL REPRODUCTION; binary fission, the placenta, contraception and reproductive health are all still taught.

The heredity half of the Exemplar unit is chapter 8, which is titled 'Heredity' rather than 'Heredity and Evolution' precisely because the evolution half was cut. Section 8.2 HEREDITY; Mendel and dominant/recessive traits are taught there.
evidence: zero hits for 'Darwin', 'speciation', 'natural selection' and 'vestigial' across all of jesc1
mappings.caveat: This is the Class 10 equivalent of the Class 9 mole note, and it is larger. Evolution - natural selection, speciation, fossils as evidence, homologous and analogous organs, human evolution - was removed by the 2023 rationalisation, and the chapter title records the removal. Exemplar questions on evolution are filed here because heredity and evolution were one chapter when the Exemplar was written, and they are on a topic this chapter no longer teaches. A student meeting them under 'Heredity' is being asked something the book does not answer. A teacher should read the unit's questions before setting them.

mappings.why: Same chapter under the same name, renumbered from 10 to 9. Spherical mirrors, the mirror formula, refraction, refractive index and the lens formula are all present.

mappings.why: Same chapter under the same name and number. 1.2 The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, 1.3 Revisiting Irrational Numbers.
mappings.caveat: Rationalisation cut two topics the Exemplar unit still tests: Euclid's division algorithm as a method for HCF, and the criterion for a terminating decimal expansion. Both survive only in the chapter's introductory paragraph, which still promises them - the sections and the two remaining exercises do not deliver them. Questions on either are correctly filed and out of syllabus.

mappings.why: Same chapter under the same name and number. 2.2 Geometrical Meaning of the Zeroes of a Polynomial, 2.3 Relationship between Zeroes and Coefficients of a Polynomial.
mappings.caveat: The division algorithm for polynomials was cut; the chapter's introduction still says it will be studied, but there is no section and no exercise for it. Exemplar questions on dividing polynomials are out of syllabus.

mappings.why: Same chapter under the same name and number. 4.2 Quadratic Equations, 4.3 Solution of a Quadratic Equation by Factorisation, 4.4 Nature of Roots.

mappings.why: Same chapter under the same name and number, and similarity - the spine of the Exemplar unit - is intact: 6.2 Similar Figures, 6.3 Similarity of Triangles, 6.4 Criteria for Similarity of Triangles.
mappings.caveat: Medium rather than high because two topics the Exemplar unit leans on were cut: the areas of similar triangles, and the Pythagoras theorem with its converse. The chapter's introduction still promises 'a simple proof of Pythagoras Theorem', but there is no section for it - it survives as a fact used, not a result proved. Exemplar questions that turn on the ratio of areas, or on proving a triangle right-angled, are out of syllabus.

mappings.why: Same chapter under the same name and number. 7.2 Distance Formula, 7.3 Section Formula.
mappings.caveat: Finding the area of a triangle from the coordinates of its vertices was cut ('area of a triangle' gets zero hits in jemh1).

mappings.why: The Exemplar unit is a superset of two current chapters, and its MCQ exercise breaks cleanly between them. EXERCISE 8.1 runs fifteen questions: Q1-Q14 are trigonometric ratios and identities, which is jemh1 ch8 (8.2 Trigonometric Ratios, 8.3 Ratios of Some Specific Angles, 8.4 Trigonometric Identities); Q15 is a heights-and-distances problem, which is ch9. The break was read off the exercise, so the exception below is a fact about it rather than a judgement about each question.
evidence: jemh108 headings 8.1-8.5, jemh109 heading 9.1 Heights and Distances
jeep208 EXERCISE 8.1 Q15: 'A pole 6 m high casts a shadow ... m long on the ground, then the Sun's ...' - the only heights-and-distances question in the exercise
mappings.caveat: Trigonometric ratios of complementary angles were cut from ch8 ('complementary angles' gets zero hits in jemh1), and several questions in this exercise are built on them - Q3, Q5, Q6 and Q7 among them. They are filed in the right chapter and are out of syllabus.
